name: scan_npm_package
description: Checks one npm package version and its whole dependency tree for known security problems. Asks OSV.dev (HTTP) about the package itself, and npm (HTTP) for its newest version, reads the dependency graph from deps.dev (gRPC), checks every dependency's licenses, advisories and deprecation in pages of 100, and asks OSV.dev for the severity and fixes of each vulnerable dependency. Returns facts only, including whether this version or the whole package is deprecated: no LLM and no side effects, so other workflows and AI agents can reuse it.

tasks.name: get_npm_latest_version
tasks.description: npm's newest version, so the scan can say whether the whole package is deprecated (the newest version is deprecated too) and give agents a version to try when the one they would recommend is deprecated. Optional: if npm doesn't answer, latestVersion is null.

tasks.name: deps_dev_get_dependencies
tasks.description: Retried up to 3 times, 2 seconds apart, by its inline taskDefinition, because calls through the deps_dev Remote Service have failed intermittently with "Missing type descriptor" errors, and a system task gets no retries without a task definition. Optional: if every try fails, the scan carries on and reports the dependency graph as missing.

inputParameters.queryExpression:
# Builds one deps.dev GetVersionBatch request covering the package and all its dependencies.
# GetDependencies returns the dependency graph as nodes: the package itself (SELF), its
# DIRECT dependencies, and their dependencies (INDIRECT). npm can install the same version
# in several places, so a version can appear many times; each one is counted and requested once.
def versionId: .versionKey.name + "@" + .versionKey.version;

(.deps.nodes // []) as $nodes
| [ $nodes[] | select(.relation == "SELF") ] as $self
| ($self | map(versionId) | .[0]) as $rootId
# One node per name@version. DIRECT nodes go first, so a version that's both counts as direct.
| (reduce (($nodes[] | select(.relation == "DIRECT")), ($nodes[] | select(.relation == "INDIRECT"))) as $node
     ({}; ($node | versionId) as $id | if $id == $rootId or .[$id] != null then . else .[$id] = $node end)
   | [ .[] ]) as $dependencies
| (.maxPackages // 5000) as $max
| {
    graphAvailable: (.deps.nodes != null),
    totalDependencies: ($dependencies | length),
    directCount: ([ $dependencies[] | select(.relation == "DIRECT") ] | length),
    indirectCount: ([ $dependencies[] | select(.relation == "INDIRECT") ] | length),
    # deps.dev accepts up to 5,000 requests per batch and returns the results 100 per page.
    requests: ([ ($self + $dependencies)[] | {versionKey} ] | .[0:$max])
  }

tasks.name: fetch_dependency_pages
tasks.description: keepLastN 2 and captureOutput false keep the loop's own output small, under Developer Edition's 2 MB limit per task: Strapi's 1,321 dependencies went over it (2.17 MB) without them. compact_dependency_page carries the running list forward, so the earlier pages aren't needed.

loopOver.name: deps_dev_get_version_batch
loopOver.description: Uses deps.dev v3alpha because GetVersionBatch only exists there; the other gRPC calls use v3. No cacheConfig on purpose: a cache key without the page token would return the first page for every page. Retried up to 3 times, 2 seconds apart, like the other deps.dev calls, because they have failed intermittently.

inputParameters.queryExpression:
# Runs once per page, inside the page loop. deps.dev returns about 1.4 KB per version (links,
# attestations, registries...), but the workflow needs only a few fields. This keeps those and
# adds them to the list from the earlier pages (.previous is the last iteration's output),
# so the full list stays small enough to pass to later tasks.
reduce (
    # The list so far...
    (.previous // [])[],
    # ...plus this page's versions, cut down to what the workflow uses. Deprecation is kept only
    # for deprecated versions (gRPC leaves out a false isDeprecated), which keeps the list small.
    ((.page.responses // [])[] | .version | select(. != null)
      | {name: .versionKey.name, version: .versionKey.version,
         licenses: (.licenses // []), advisories: [ (.advisoryKeys // [])[] | .id ]}
        + (if .isDeprecated == true then {deprecated: true, deprecatedReason: (.deprecatedReason // "")} else {} end))
  ) as $v
  # Keyed by name@version, so a page that's processed twice (on a retry) adds no duplicates.
  ({}; .[$v.name + "@" + $v.version] = $v)
| {versions: [ .[] ]}

# Lists the dependencies that have known advisories, so the next loop can look each one up
# on OSV.dev for severity and fixes. Most advisories first, at most maxLookups of them.
.rootRef as $root
| (.maxLookups // 40) as $max
| [ (.versions // [])[]
    | select((.name + "@" + .version) != $root)   # the package's own advisories come from OSV directly
    | select((.advisories // []) != [])
    | {name, version, advisoryCount: (.advisories | length), ids: .advisories} ]
| sort_by(-.advisoryCount)
| {
    vulnerableCount: length,
    # Numbered from 1 to match the loop's iteration numbers, so build_evidence_pack can
    # pair each dependency with its lookup result.
    lookups: (.[0:$max] | reduce .[] as $dep ([]; . + [$dep + {iteration: (length + 1)}]))
  }

tasks.name: lookup_dependency_advisories
tasks.description: No keepLastN on purpose: summarize_scan pairs the Nth vulnerable dependency with iteration N of this loop, so every iteration's output has to be kept. It runs at most 40 times (maxLookups in find_vulnerable_dependencies), so the output stays bounded.

inputParameters.queryExpression:
# summarize_scan: the last step of scan_npm_package. Turns the raw OSV.dev and deps.dev answers
# into security facts about a package version and its whole dependency tree. No LLM is involved,
# so other workflows (or AI agents) can reuse these facts directly.
#
# Inputs:  .packageName, .packageVersion
#          .osv                OSV.dev's answer for the package itself (null if that call failed)
#          .dependencyScan     counts from build_dependency_batch
#          .dependencyVersions one record per version ({name, version, licenses, advisories}, plus
#                              deprecated and deprecatedReason when deprecated), from the page loop
#          .vulnerableDeps     the list from find_vulnerable_dependencies
#          .dependencyLookups  the OSV lookup loop's output (item N is iteration N)
#          .npmLatest          npm's manifest of the newest version (null if that call failed)
# Output:  {sources, advisories, upgrade, deprecation, transitiveDependencies, dependencyLicenses}

# ---- Helpers: versions ----

# "4.17.1" -> [4, 17, 1], so versions compare correctly as arrays.
# Pre-release and build tags are dropped ("5.0.0-beta.3" -> [5, 0, 0]), so a pre-release
# fix counts as its final release. A part that isn't a number counts as 0.
def semver:
  split("+")[0] | split("-")[0] | split(".")
  | map(if test("^[0-9]+$") then tonumber else 0 end);

# ---- Helpers: advisories and fixes (OSV.dev data) ----

# An OSV advisory describes the affected versions as ranges of events: a range starts at an
# "introduced" version and ends at a "fixed" version (or just after "last_affected").
# These are the ranges for package $name. Ranges of git commits are skipped.
def rangesFor($name):
  [ (.affected // [])[] | select(.package.name == $name) | (.ranges // [])[] | select(.type != "GIT") ];

# Is version $v (a semver array) inside this range? Yes if the range was introduced at or
# before $v and wasn't fixed between that point and $v.
def rangeIncludes($v):
  (.events // []) as $events
  | any($events[] | .introduced // empty | semver | select(. <= $v);
      . as $start
      | (any($events[] | .fixed // empty | semver; . > $start and . <= $v) | not)
        and (any($events[] | .last_affected // empty | semver; . >= $start and . < $v) | not));

# Does this advisory affect version $v of package $name?
def affects($name; $v): any(rangesFor($name)[]; rangeIncludes($v));

# Input: the advisories that affect version $current of package $name.
# Output: {status, version}. The version is the lowest one above $current that none of the
# advisories affect, preferring the current major version, or null if there isn't one.
# The answer is always one of the advisories' "fixed" versions, because that's where a range ends.
def fixTarget($name; $current):
  . as $advisories
  | ($current | semver) as $cur
  # For each advisory, every fixed version above the current one.
  | [ $advisories[] | [ rangesFor($name)[] | (.events // [])[] | .fixed // empty | semver | select(. > $cur) ] ] as $fixesPerAdvisory
  | ([ $fixesPerAdvisory[][] ] | unique) as $candidates
  # The candidates that no advisory affects, lowest first.
  | [ $candidates[] | select(. as $c | any($advisories[]; affects($name; $c)) | not) ] as $safe
  | (($safe | map(select(.[0] == $cur[0])) | .[0]) // $safe[0]) as $target
  | (if $target == null then null else $target | map(tostring) | join(".") end) as $version
  | if ($advisories | length) == 0 then {status: "none_needed", version: null}
    elif any($fixesPerAdvisory[]; length == 0) then {status: "no_fix", version: null}
    elif $target == null then {status: "no_single_fix", version: null}
    elif $target[0] == $cur[0] then {status: "same_major", version: $version}
    else {status: "major_upgrade", version: $version} end;

# How a fix reads in the evidence and in the brief.
def fixText:
  if .status == "same_major" then "fixed in " + .version + " (same major version)"
  elif .status == "major_upgrade" then "fixed in " + .version + " (new major version)"
  elif .status == "no_fix" then "no fixed version yet"
  elif .status == "no_single_fix" then "no single version fixes every advisory"
  else "fix details unavailable" end;

# ---- Helpers: severity and text ----

# GitHub's severity labels, most severe first. Anything else, or no label, ranks 0.
def severityRank:
  if . == "CRITICAL" then 4 elif . == "HIGH" then 3 elif . == "MODERATE" then 2 elif . == "LOW" then 1 else 0 end;

# ["HIGH", "MODERATE", "HIGH"] -> "2 HIGH, 1 MODERATE"
def severitySummary:
  . as $all
  | [ ("CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MODERATE", "LOW") as $level
      | ($all | map(select(. == $level)) | length) as $n | select($n > 0)
      | ($n | tostring) + " " + $level ]
    + [ ($all | map(select(severityRank == 0)) | length) as $n | select($n > 0)
      | ($n | tostring) + " of unknown severity" ]
  | join(", ");

# Cut long text to $max characters, marking the cut with "…".
def shorten($max): if length > $max then .[0:$max] + "…" else . end;

# ---- Inputs ----

.packageName as $name
| .packageVersion as $version
| ($name + "@" + $version) as $rootRef
| (.dependencyScan // {}) as $scan               # dependency counts from build_dependency_batch
# One record per dependency version ({name, version, licenses, advisories}), from the page loop.
| [ (.dependencyVersions // [])[] | select((.name + "@" + .version) != $rootRef) ] as $dependencies
# The package's own record from the same batch, for its deprecation (null if deps.dev had no data).
| ([ (.dependencyVersions // [])[] | select((.name + "@" + .version) == $rootRef) ] | .[0]) as $rootVersion

# ---- The package's own advisories and its upgrade target ----

| (.osv.vulns // []) as $ownAdvisories
| ($ownAdvisories | fixTarget($name; $version)) as $ownFix
| ($ownAdvisories | length) as $ownCount
| (if $ownCount == 1 then "the advisory" elif $ownCount == 2 then "both advisories"
   else "all " + ($ownCount | tostring) + " advisories" end) as $fixesWhat


# ---- Dependency advisories, with severity and fixes from OSV.dev ----

# find_vulnerable_dependencies listed the dependencies that have advisories, and the
# lookup_dependency_advisories loop asked OSV.dev about each one: item N is iteration N.
| (.vulnerableDeps.lookups // []) as $lookups
| (.dependencyLookups // {}) as $lookupResults
| [ $lookups[] as $dep
    | ($lookupResults[($dep.iteration | tostring)].osv_dependency_ref.response.body) as $osv
    # Match each advisory ID from deps.dev to its OSV record (by ID or alias).
    | [ $dep.ids[] as $id
        | ([ ($osv.vulns // [])[] | select(.id == $id or any((.aliases // [])[]; . == $id)) ] | .[0]) as $record
        | {id: $id,
           severity: ($record.database_specific.severity // "UNKNOWN"),
           summary: ($record.summary // "" | shorten(120)),
           record: $record} ] as $advisories
    # The lowest version of the dependency that fixes all its advisories. Unknown if the
    # lookup failed or any advisory has no OSV record.
    | (if $osv == null or any($advisories[]; .record == null) then {status: "unknown", version: null}
       else [ $advisories[].record ] | fixTarget($dep.name; $dep.version) end) as $fix
    | {
        package: ($dep.name + "@" + $dep.version),
        advisoryCount: $dep.advisoryCount,
        severity: ([ $advisories[].severity ] | severitySummary),
        highOrCritical: ([ $advisories[] | select(.severity | severityRank >= 3) ] | length),
        fixedIn: $fix.version,
        fixAvailable: (if $fix.status == "unknown" then null else $fix.version != null end),
        fix: ($fix | fixText),
        # Up to 10 advisories, most severe first.
        advisories: ([ $advisories[] | {id, severity, summary} ] | sort_by(-(.severity | severityRank)) | .[0:10]),
        # Used only for the totals and the sort order below.
        allAdvisories: [ $advisories[] | {id, severity} ],
        rank: ([ $advisories[].severity | severityRank ] | max)
      } ] as $enriched
# Totals across all dependencies. An advisory shared by several dependencies counts once.
| ([ $dependencies[] | select(.advisories != []) ] | length) as $vulnerableCount
| ([ $enriched[].allAdvisories[] ] | reduce .[] as $a ({}; .[$a.id] = $a.severity) | [ .[] ]) as $depSeverities
# Complete only if every vulnerable dependency was looked up, and every lookup worked.
| (($lookups | length) == $vulnerableCount and all($enriched[]; .fixAvailable != null)) as $severityComplete
# The advisories in the dependencies, counted once each, e.g. 38 for @strapi/strapi@5.58.0.
| ([ $dependencies[].advisories[] ] | unique | length) as $depAdvisoryCount
# How the dependencies' advisories get fixed, for the upgrade explanation, e.g. "38 advisories in its
# dependencies are listed separately, and are fixed by updating those packages, except in
# deepmerge@4.3.1, which has no known fix". "No known fix" covers both no fix and a failed lookup.
| [ $enriched[] | select(.fixAvailable != true) | .package ] as $unfixed
| (if ($unfixed | length) > 3 then ($unfixed | .[0:3] | join(", ")) + " and " + (($unfixed | length) - 3 | tostring) + " more"
   else $unfixed | join(", ") end) as $unfixedText
| (if ($unfixed | length) == 1 then "has" else "have" end) as $has
| (if ($enriched | length) == 1 then "that package" else "those packages" end) as $those
| (if $depAdvisoryCount == 1 then "1 advisory in its dependencies is listed separately, and is"
   else ($depAdvisoryCount | tostring) + " advisories in its dependencies are listed separately, and are" end) as $listed
| (if $depAdvisoryCount == 0 then ""
   elif $unfixed == [] then $listed + " fixed by updating " + $those
   elif ($unfixed | length) == ($enriched | length) then $listed + " not fixed yet: " + $unfixedText + " " + $has + " no known fix"
   else $listed + " fixed by updating " + $those + ", except in " + $unfixedText + ", which " + $has + " no known fix" end) as $depAdvisoryNote

# ---- The scan's facts ----

| {
    # Which sources answered. assess_npm_package lists the ones that didn't as missing.
    sources: {
        osv: (.osv != null),
        dependencyGraph: ($scan.graphAvailable // false),
        versionBatch: ((.dependencyVersions // []) != []),
        dependencyAdvisoryDetails: (all($enriched[]; .fixAvailable != null)),
        npmLatest: (.npmLatest.version != null)
    },
    # Computed here, so the LLM never does version arithmetic.
    upgrade: (
      if .osv == null then
        {status: "unknown", recommendedVersion: null, explanation: "advisory data from OSV.dev is unavailable, so no upgrade target could be computed"}
      elif $ownFix.status == "none_needed" then
        # About the package itself only, so say so: its dependencies can still have advisories,
        # e.g. "no advisories affect express itself, so it needs no upgrade; 11 advisories in its
        # dependencies are listed separately, and are fixed by updating those packages"
        {status: "none_needed", recommendedVersion: null,
         explanation: ("no advisories affect " + $name + " itself, so it needs no upgrade"
           + (if $depAdvisoryNote == "" then "" else "; " + $depAdvisoryNote end))}
      elif $ownFix.status == "no_fix" then
        {status: "no_fix", recommendedVersion: null, explanation: ("at least one advisory on " + $name + " has no fixed version yet")}
      elif $ownFix.status == "no_single_fix" then
        {status: "no_single_fix", recommendedVersion: null, explanation: ("no single version fixes every advisory on " + $name)}
      else
        {status: $ownFix.status,
         recommendedVersion: $ownFix.version,
         explanation: ((if $ownFix.status == "same_major" then "the lowest " + (($version | semver)[0] | tostring) + ".x release"
                        else "the lowest release, in major version " + ($ownFix.version | split(".")[0]) + "," end)
                       + " that fixes " + $fixesWhat + " on " + $name + "; re-run this review on that version to check its dependencies")}
      end),
    advisories: [ $ownAdvisories[] | {
        id,
        summary,
        severity: (.database_specific.severity // "UNKNOWN"),
        fixedIn: ([ rangesFor($name)[] | (.events // [])[] | .fixed // empty ] | unique),
        # True if one of those fixes is newer than the version under review.
        hasFix: any(rangesFor($name)[] | (.events // [])[] | .fixed // empty | semver; . > ($version | semver))
    } ],
    # Whether this version is deprecated (deps.dev), and npm's newest version. If that's deprecated
    # too, the maintainers have deprecated the whole package. Agents use latestVersion as a version
    # to try when the one they'd recommend is deprecated, e.g. for lodash@4.18.0:
    # {thisVersion: true, reason: "Bad release. Please use lodash@4.17.21 instead.", latestVersion: "4.18.1", latestDeprecated: false}
    deprecation: {
        thisVersion: (if $rootVersion == null then null else ($rootVersion.deprecated // false) end),
        reason: ($rootVersion.deprecatedReason // null),
        latestVersion: (.npmLatest.version // null),
        latestDeprecated: (if .npmLatest.version == null then null
                           else ((.npmLatest.deprecated | type) == "string" and .npmLatest.deprecated != "") end)
    },
    transitiveDependencies: {
        total: ($scan.totalDependencies // 0),
        direct: ($scan.directCount // 0),
        indirect: ($scan.indirectCount // 0),
        checked: ($dependencies | length),
        uniqueAdvisoryCount: ([ $dependencies[].advisories[] ] | unique | length),
        packagesWithAdvisoriesCount: $vulnerableCount,
        advisorySeverity: ($depSeverities | severitySummary),
        highOrCriticalAdvisories: ($depSeverities | map(select(severityRank >= 3)) | length),
        severityComplete: $severityComplete,
        unfixedHighOrCritical: [ $enriched[] | select(.highOrCritical > 0 and .fixAvailable == false) | .package ],
        # Deprecated dependencies, e.g. {count: 1, packages: ["node-domexception@1.0.0"]} (up to 10 listed).
        deprecated: ([ $dependencies[] | select(.deprecated == true) | (.name + "@" + .version) ]
                     | {count: length, packages: .[0:10]}),
        # The 15 most severe, for the LLM and the brief.
        packagesWithAdvisories: ($enriched | sort_by([-.rank, -.advisoryCount]) | .[0:15]
            | map({package, advisoryCount, severity, highOrCritical, fixedIn, fixAvailable, fix, advisories})),
        # How many dependencies use each license (multiple expressions joined with " + ").
        licenseCounts: (reduce ($dependencies[] | .licenses | if . == [] then "<none>" else join(" + ") end) as $l
                          ({}; .[$l] = ((.[$l] // 0) + 1)))
    },
    # Every dependency's licenses, for the license policy in assess_npm_package.
    dependencyLicenses: [ $dependencies[] | {package: (.name + "@" + .version), licenses} ]
  }
